identity.name: Triammonium citrate
identity.chemical_class: Citrate salt (ammonium salt of citric acid)

secondary_categories: flavor enhancer (related dibasic ammonium citrate entry in CFR)
function.mechanism: Acts as a citrate/ammonium buffer to adjust food pH; citrate anion also contributes weak metal-ion complexation.

adi.basis: No EFSA ADI value identified in the current EFSA re-evaluation status table row for E380; no EFSA opinion link is populated there.

efsa.key_finding: E380 is listed as a permitted additive, but the EFSA re-evaluation status row indicates re-evaluation not completed and no adoption/publication date or EFSA opinion link (status table dated 18 Feb 2026).

adi.basis: ADI = NOT LIMITED; included in the ADI for citric acid and bases.

concerns.summary: Evidence gap: no completed EFSA re-evaluation opinion entry was found for E380 in the latest published status table, and modern E380-specific toxicology literature is sparse.
Theoretical concern only: as an ammonium salt, very high exposure could be less desirable in people with severe ammonia-handling impairment, but no direct E380 clinical risk dataset was identified.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA lists ADI as NOT LIMITED (1979) and includes triammonium citrate within the citric acid and bases ADI framework.
No specific IARC Monographs classification entry was identified for triammonium citrate or CAS 3458-72-8 in the current IARC list dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA ADI is not limited, so a numeric ADI exceedance calculation is not applicable from that source.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current evidence supports low concern at intended use levels (JECFA ADI not limited; no IARC signal), but confidence is moderated by incomplete/unclear EFSA re-evaluation closure for E380 and sparse modern direct toxicology evidence.
key_factors: JECFA ADI is NOT LIMITED (evaluation year 1979).
EU status table lists E380 as permitted but re-evaluation row is not marked completed and lacks opinion link/date entries.
FDA CFR has a GRAS entry for related ammonium citrate dibasic under cGMP conditions.
No specific IARC classification entry found for triammonium citrate.
